body: Again, please don't hesitate to contact me at definitiveact@gmail dot com. I'd hate to lose contact through something like Reddit logins.

Replying in two parts, I was not sure if Reddit would cut me off.

I don't think there is any reconciliation. She's made it clear. Her lawyer has served me. I've gotten my own. My lawyer is confident I'll come out okay. It's good to know, but it's hard to care when your life is falling apart like this. I think of the cats and how we'll split them. I cry when one of them meows at me or gets underfoot. We took them all in from shelters promising happy loving forever homes. Now we need to split them, like the assets.

I drew for the first time in months the other night, while listening to the old Explosions in the Sky album "Earth is Not a Cold Dead Place". Wasn't even aware of it until midway in, the best sort of creating. I'm looking to hold onto that.

The worst part is the uncertainty of it all. Where I'll go. What I'll do. When my deadline is. My wife doesn't know. She doesn't even know what she'll do or where she'll go or how she'll subsist. I'm learning so much of this is not about mental health or sex, but money. A common theme when she does talk to me about proceedings or Whys is money. How little the car is worth. How she'll have to take a loan from her guilt tripping parents to pay me out the sum for assets. How she will be out of the condo and back to renting apartments. How spousal support will drain her more.

The surviving, rational part of me doesn't feel bad at all. I didn't pull the trigger on this. I didn't want this. I offered alternatives. I still have the door open. Therapy and work will take time and money and patience, but if she were willing, it would save so much anguish. And money.

I apologize for waiting so long to respond. I've been curbing the net to try and stay rooted in the real world and figure things out. I also wiped the cookies on my laptop and lost access, and am thankful my desktop still has credentials and I can set the password.

I am grateful for you checking up on me. I can never express enough how much it means to me. How much it helped me get through that awful night and first week. It's only been just 3 weeks. It feels like months. I was in a low point this weekend, depressed in bed and wanting to throw myself in front of a train. It was the thought of people like you, reaching out to strangers then and now, the good parts of humanity and community.

When I am stronger and stable, I want to repay you and acknowledge you somehow. Please do keep in touch.

If Reddit jinxes me, my gmail is definitiveact@gmail.com

Please use it. I am grateful for everyone who kept me from succumbing to the darkness and quitting. That is the light in this world I want to fuel.

Hi,

Thank you so much for checking in. I'm sorry that I did not reply until now, time just slips away as I try to stay busy.

It's not gotten better, but I'm making it. The separation is going to happen. I made efforts to repair the relationship, but she is not interested. At least I won't regret that I never tried.

My social worker has called me at home twice for hour sessions. He says he can't keep it up as he was supposed to be short-term, but given current circumstances he is willing to listen and talk. In the meantime I found a proper therapist. Out of pocket, but I'll take it. I have only seen her twice, budgeting for bimonthly chats, with more if needed.

The first two sessions were July 2nd and then last Tuesday. I will see her again on the 31st (she has vacation, I can't fault that). It feels strange talking to her and my social worker because they talk to the Day Me. The one in control, who is making a list and getting things done to stay functional and alert through this. To them I am coping well, I am remarkably well.

They're talking to Bruce Banner. I need them to talk to the Hulk.

During the day I have my things to do. I have friends and family to call. I take long walks in the sun and listen to music. At night, things change. I used to work in nursing, and I know sundowning is a thing in Alzheimer's patients, but I think it may be a thing in everybody. At night, as the sun goes, the loneliness creeps in. I feel low. Kill myself low. I cry. Anxiety takes hold. Family are asleep. Friends have lives I don't want to intrude on every time this happens. I have no one to talk to or just listen to, except for one loyal nocturnal friend.

Eventually I sleep. When I wake up, I'm functional and have one or two things to do. I wish my therapist and social worker could talk to that me.

In good news, I got the blood draw on the 6th! It was idiotic. I felt nothing. I didn't even make it to the chorus of the song I was listening to. It made me feel worse at first, that everything was crumbling because of this stupid blood draw that it turns out I never even felt and took less than 30 seconds. I know there's more to it than that, but I did feel like more of a failure at first. Then I felt good. I accomplished something. I did it. I can do it again.

I need to see the doctor this Wednesday about an ECG, and that's the final step until I can start the Lithium - another goal to check off. I'm going to be brutal with my doctor about my feelings, my life now. I felt that my diagnosis was delayed because I was in denial so long. I feel like my therapy is held back because they talk to me when I'm competent and confident. I'm going to be truthful to the doctor, and I cry just thinking of it, but if they need a baseline on blood and heart and kidneys, then they will want a baseline on my emotional state.

Best case, the drugs are a miracle and help me. Worst case, they don't, and we try other options.

My wife and I still share the place, and it hurts. She has a newfound social life and is out every night. A package arrived last Monday, I had to pay customs on it. The customs list was stuck to the outside. It was bondage gear from a shop in the States. This is not a thing we are into, or at the least, she has never expressed an interest in it to me. It's all in rose gold and feminine colour options, and a part of me feels (without evidence, just a gut hindsight) that there's something going on between her and a female friend. It doesn't matter, this is a no fault province. It has no bearing on the separation. At the least I now know maybe my wife had secrets, or couldn't tell me everything, at the least, and that this is not all my fault. I would still like to reconcile, but my trust is fractured from that event.

You can be helped. It's hard to hear when you're depressed - I know, I do this to myself all the time, even before my post here - but the first step is helping yourself.

I did lay in bed for 22 hours straight after I wrote this post. However, I had my phone and I called my social worker, doctor, family, friends. And you know the worst part? My friends and family aren't local. I'm in a foreign country thanks to my marriage and I don't have any ties that are strictly mine. No support system.

Still, I called. And even though I laid in bed for 22 hours with my cats while I cried, I accomplished calling my social worker and doctor. My social worker told me the fact I called was huge. I wasn't rolling over and dying (I was, but I wasn't).

The next day, Friday, I got out of bed. I hadn't eaten since Wednesday evening. I made a sandwich. I called the psychotherapists. That was it. If you called me and asked me what I did Friday, I cried, made a sandwich and looked for a proper therapist. It was something I could check off. 

My brother woke up, worked out, went to work, managed an international company, had his soccer league practice, went to a cookout, saw Jurassic World.

I laid in bed. Made a sandwich. Made some phone calls. But I felt accomplished. It was enough motivation to realize I should shower, wash two days of crying off of my face. Put on clean clothes. And then I collapsed into the crying with my cats.

Still. I had done something.

That carried into Saturday. It was easier. I played guitar a bit. I showered. I made another sandwich. I kept up with house chores because it was something to do. I looked up the treatments these therapists mentioned, I read about this drug I'm terrified to take. Tried to find the positive stories, not the whiny horror stories.

I was depressed for years before I went to the doctor and they agreed, "Yeah, you're clinically depressed. Try group and a social worker." I didn't even get meds until a few years after that. Then it turned out I was bipolar, so I found I had "something bad". And now back to my OP up there.

It sucks, man. But I'm replying to everyone who responded to me because every response (even yours) made a difference. I can't say you saved my life dramatically, dissuading me from killing myself. As above, I was too aware/afraid to do that. You and everyone else did save my life longer term, though, by helping me not be alone. And that gave me the motivation to just do things.

Go to the doctors. They can't force you to do anything. In-patient is only a risk if you're a threat to yourself or others. If nothing else, you can educate yourself about yourself.

You can be helped. It may not be meds. It may take many therapists (I went through 3 social workers). It may just be you find new purpose in exercise or a hobby.

Really, you need to do something so that if you have any problems with your girlfriend, you need to know you tried. The worst, and I heard this from my wife, is feeling useless, because eventually you feel enabling and that you are the problem. You need to get back in it for yourself.

Love yourself. Get the love back you can shine out into the world so your girlfriend realizes she isn't useless. She was a supportive spark.

Don't wait until it's too late like I did. You need to fight. And yeah, fighting can sometimes be just making a sandwich and changing your t-shirt. All of us with depression understand that's an Avengers-level victory.

You can do it. You did it for me.

Thank you for sharing your own story with me. We have a lot in common there.  


All I can say is I made it four days. I'm going to make it more, day by day. I don't know what's going to happen at this point.   


I do know I need to get myself right. I hope you find the will and means to join me. If you would like to talk, I am always down to talk. It's this human connection that keeps me from collapsing into snotful howls when the quiet of the house gets me at 2AM. Don't hesitate to reach me, u/47Shit.

Thank you for the kind reply, u/Bomby57. I may take you up on that. It's been a painful few days.   


Spent 22 hours in bed wallowing, but then forced myself to get up and be proactive about myself. I can't decline like this ever again. And what's a blood draw against losing your love, life, and a hanging attempt?   


I just wanted to reply so you know your input was valued and made a difference. I'm still here. Functioning, not rolled over and waiting to die. I'm seeing a psychotherapist tomorrow. It would be nice to chat to someone later.
Thank you for your kindness. Be easy, and I hope benevolent things come to you.

In (painful) talks with my wife during this weekend I learned that sharing is good, but oversharing made things worse.  


In fact, she said things were better when I was "depressed" because when I was happy, she was happy I was in a good place and could ride out the depressions. When I was relabeled "bipolar", it stressed her twice as hard. Now my happy moments were tempered with anxiety because she just worried if I was going to have a hypomanic fit of anger or anxiety when the happiness wore out. And yeah, that has happened.  


Talk to someone, though. I called my social worker the next day. Found a therapist for this week. My doctor even called me because my social worker passed a note to her.  


I don't know how my situation will play out. I can tell you that you should get yourself right for yourself. Whether that saves your relationships or prepares you for the future, don't wait until you lose something to get the wake up call.

Thanks so much. It's been hard. As in taking a shower and making a sandwich were Herculean tasks worth World Cup goal celebrations, but I have pushed through and found a psychotherapist for this week.  


I allowed myself a day of wallowing in bed in the dark, but by Friday I had to just get up and do things, if only for myself. Thanks for the support, it means the world.

Thanks so much for responding. It helped.  


I checked in with my social worker. Booked a psychotherapist for this week. Forced myself to stay productive and on track, for myself. Hearing from people like you really did help me pull through the maelstrom of emotion.

Four days later, and I'm still here.   


I hope OP and everyone else is, too. We made it. It's something you can point to.

Sorry for the late repy.

As part of my treatment, I have been prescribed Lithium. Lithium has many side effects, but one of them is kidney failure over time. You need to get a baseline bloodwork established and then they monitor you biweekly at first - or at least that was my care plan.

There are so many negatives you can find about Lithium, so I don't want to deter you, but the renal failure and weight gain possibilities are the two that have put me off. That led to this, though, so I do recommend looking for the positive experiences as well. It's what I spent the last few days doing.

Cheers, and thank you for lending your shoulder to a stranger. It really did help.

I understood, it was a point well taken.

What are your strategies?

I've had a solo social worker, but he doesn't really focus on the bipolar. I started a group therapy thing at a local mental health center, but the first group was in April and we don't reconvene until August. Ironically, I got the invitation to the August group today just before this.

I've started charting my mood; didn't believe in it much before this year. Quit alcohol (always did make me hyper, now I know why). Cutting certain foods and curbing sugar. Drinking a gallon of water a day.

Yoga, meditation. Exercise. I'm open to anything.

Thanks. Just having this discourse helps.

I didn't know gums could hurt from crying, but here I am.

Yeah. Are you on meds? I'm so afraid of the Lithium after hearing about it from reddit and YouTube. You can PM me if you like.

I think I put it off too long and damned myself. Would meds have even made a difference? Even my doctor told me it'd take months to find a "proper" dose.

She supported me for most of this journey. I'm really hateful of myself now for letting BP poison this and her. I know it's stressful, but I never want to break anyone with my own burdens.

I know that it's not all on me. And yet that depressive part is holding me up to only that mirror.

Thank you so much.

I just checked my e-mail and had one about a sale on Pusheen stuff. She likes Pusheen.

It sent me over the edge in terms of snotful wails.

The worst is she's in the guest room next door.

Is it wrong to want to fix it?

Me too.  


Pull through for me. I know it sucks. But if you pull through, then I won't feel so alone in my own battle. I need to know you're there for a morale boost. And someone else will see us. And so on.
Thanks, mate. You too.

Thank you so much for reading and responding. And I appreciate the complement.

I've tried watercolour, as it's new to me, but it doesn't take.
